name: Tata Consultancy Services Ltd
title: Tata Consultancy Services Ltd - 532540 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: IT services demand is soft with client deferrals, and margins fell 130 bps to 24% on wage hikes, but management still reads the call as an AI-led deal-win recovery in Q2; no capacity signals as this is an IT services business.

summary.headline: TCS Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13.9% YoY to ₹72,275 crore, but operating margin fell 130 bps QoQ to 24% on wage hikes.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was ₹72,275 crore, up 2.2% QoQ and 13.9% YoY in rupee terms, and the fourth consecutive quarter of growth. In dollar terms revenue was $7,624 million, flat QoQ and up 2.7% YoY; constant currency growth was 0.4% QoQ and 3.2% YoY. TCV was $9.5 billion, including an $800 million mega deal with SKF. Operating margin fell to 24% (down 130 bps QoQ), with a 170 bps hit from annual salary increments partly offset by 40 bps of currency benefit and efficiencies. Management said clients deferred some projects amid geopolitical uncertainty and expects demand to improve sometime in Q2.

segments.name: BFSI
segments.commentary: Delivered good growth across geographies; management remains optimistic on sustained BFSI growth.

segments.name: Technology, Software and Services
segments.commentary: Continued growth momentum with several large and mid-sized wins, including a multi-million-dollar ServiceNow deal.

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: Softness in auto; management expects a turnaround in Q2 based on net new wins including SKF, ABB and a Fortune 50 European firm.

segments.name: Life Sciences and Healthcare
segments.commentary: Declined this quarter; management expects recovery, with some verticals showing an uptick.

segments.name: Consumer Business Group
segments.commentary: Pressured by inflation and geopolitics affecting discretionary spend; airlines in North America and non-essential retail under stress.

segments.name: CMI and ERU
segments.commentary: CMI saw modest growth amid industry headwinds; ERU declined slightly, with management positive on AI infrastructure, electrification and renewables.

segments.name: Regional Markets
segments.commentary: Growth driven by India, public services, and products and platforms.

guidance_outlook: No formal revenue or earnings guidance given; management expects demand to resume sometime in Q2 FY27 due to pent-up technology backlog.
Management aims to progressively move margins closer to at least FY26 levels, with an exit at 25% plus in the quarter and a target to achieve it sooner rather than later.
Management expects Manufacturing and Life Sciences to turn around in Q2, tech services to keep growing, and Consumer to recover once geopolitical sentiment improves.
Capital allocation policy unchanged; continued commitment to returning substantial free cash flows to shareholders.
Productivity pass-through to clients is about 10% to 15% on average, front-loaded in contracts, with the aim of offsetting it through new opportunities.
capex_capacity: Investing in AI capabilities, talent transformation, partner ecosystems, platforms, domain solutions and go-to-market capacity; no capex figures disclosed.
Launched TCS SovereignSecure Cloud for Europe to address data residency and sovereign cloud demand.
Launched a dedicated Global Value and Innovation Center business unit to build, operate, transform or divest global capability centers.
Anthropic partnership includes 50,000 licenses; TCS is first GSI partner for Mistral AI with a dedicated COE for industry solutions.
demand_pricing: Clients deferred some projects in Q1 as geopolitical uncertainty rose from March and continued through June; management is optimistic on a Q2 demand recovery.
TCV of $9.5 billion including SKF ($800 million, net new) and the sixth mega deal in five quarters; three mega deals announced in the last quarter per management.
AI revenue growth was lumpy: incremental AI revenue added was $75 million in Q1 versus $125 million in Q4, with management saying AI projects are often one- to two-quarter engagements.
Engagement models are shifting; agentic GBS deals saw more outcome-based commitments in F&A, HR and customer experience.
Productivity gains passed to clients are about 10% to 15% on average, typically offset by additional client work according to management.
Management said it sees no broad white-collar contraction and that total headcount rose in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How much did macro and geopolitical uncertainty affect Q1, and what is the September quarter outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said uncertainty rose from March and clients deferred projects; it is optimistic demand will resume sometime in Q2 on pent-up technology backlog, with no rate of change quantified.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the roughly 16% YoY dollar increase in SG&A?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said cost categories were refined and the COR/SG&A split was removed; investments are in talent, partnerships and targeted areas, including some M&A-related charges.

qa_highlights.question: Is AI-driven productivity deflating revenue, and how much has been passed through?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is hard to quantify; in most places productivity passed on is about 10% to 15%, and customers often give additional work in return.

qa_highlights.question: Why is incremental AI revenue lower QoQ, and is there seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI work is non-recurring and project-based, so quarterly revenue will be lumpy, though the trend is rising and client conversations are yielding opportunities.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins fall sharply across segments, and when will they recover?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the 170 bps wage impact is the main driver across segments, with some vertical-level investment; TCS typically takes the Q1 headwind and aims to exit at 25%+ margin.

qa_highlights.question: How many freshers were hired and what is the plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 14,000 campus graduates were onboarded last quarter, and hiring is ongoing with a focus on AI-native skills.

risks_watch: Whether the Q2 demand recovery materialises given ongoing geopolitical conflicts and project deferrals.
Margin recovery: the 170 bps wage impact and continued investment versus the stated goal of exiting at 25%+ and approaching FY26 levels.
Consumer and Life Sciences softness; management did not give a timeline beyond Q2 for consumer recovery.
AI revenue lumpiness (incremental $75 million in Q1 vs $125 million in Q4) and whether net-new AI deals convert to revenue quickly.
Productivity pass-through to clients (10% to 15%) could compress revenue per deal over time.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term AI strategy and deal wins, but cautious on near-term demand, acknowledging geopolitical deferrals and declining consumer and life sciences segments. Management was somewhat evasive on quantifying the rate of demand change and on productivity pass-through and the $1 trillion spend contraction question.
key_quotes: I expect the demand to improve sometime in Q2.
Our operating margins stood at 24%, down 130 bps sequentially, primarily due to wage hikes.
We want to exit at 25% plus and strive to achieve it sooner rather than later.
In most places, the productivity gain passed on is around 10% to 15% range.

growth.why: No formal revenue guidance; management expects demand to improve in Q2 FY27 and exit operating margin at 25%+, backed by a $9.5B TCV (incl. $800M SKF deal) but no capacity additions, and constant-currency growth was only 0.4% QoQ and 3.2% YoY.
